claims.text: The patient is at 36 hours of age with a negative blood culture, which aligns with the guideline recommendation to have culture results available at this time to facilitate timely treatment decisions.

Because the baby is 36+0 weeks gestation and has a negative blood culture but requires antibiotics for more than 36 hours due to strong initial clinical suspicion, the guideline suggests considering a switch from intravenous to oral antibiotics to complete the course.

A switch to oral antibiotics is only appropriate if the baby's clinical condition is reassuring, with no current clinical indicators of ongoing infection, and if the levels and trends of C-reactive protein concentration are reassuring.
In addition to clinical and laboratory reassurance, the baby must be tolerating oral feeds before switching from intravenous to oral antibiotics can be considered.

If intravenous antibiotics are continued for longer than 36 hours despite negative blood cultures, the need for ongoing antibiotics must be reviewed at least once every 24 hours, taking into account the level of initial clinical suspicion, the baby's clinical progress, and CRP trends.

The specific criteria for stopping antibiotics at 48 hours (negative culture, low initial suspicion, reassuring clinical condition, and reassuring CRP trends) apply to late-onset infection, not early-onset, and therefore do not directly apply to this 36-hour-old patient with suspected EOS.

packet.evaluation_question: At 36 hours, culture is negative but symptoms persist. Explain the missing criteria for stopping antibiotics.

evidence.text: For babies given antibiotics because of suspected late-onset infection, consider stopping the antibiotics at 48 hours if: • the blood culture is negative and • the initial clinical suspicion of infection was not strong and • the baby's clinical condition is reassuring, with no clinical indicators of possible infection and • the levels and trends of C‑reactive protein concentration are reassuring. [2021]

Consider establishing hospital systems to provide blood culture results 36 hours after starting antibiotics for early-onset neonatal infection, to allow timely stopping of treatment and discharge from hospital. [2012]

When continuing intravenous antibiotics for longer than 36 hours despite negative blood cultures, review the need for ongoing antibiotics at least once every 24 hours, taking account of: • the level of initial clinical suspicion of infection and • the baby's clinical progress and current condition and • the levels and trends of C-reactive protein concentration. [2012] 1.22 Switching to oral antibiotics

For babies born from 35+0 weeks' gestation with negative blood culture who need antibiotics for more than 36 hours because the initial clinical suspicion of infection was strong, consider switching treatment from intravenous to oral antibiotics at 36 hours or thereafter to complete the course (up to 7 days of antibiotics in total) if: • the baby's clinical condition is reassuring, with no current clinical indicators of ongoing infection (see box 2 for clinical indicators of possible early-onset neonatal infection) and • the levels and trends of C-reactive protein concentration are reassuring and • the baby is tolerating oral feeds. [2026]
